title: Odd String Difference
summary: Given an array of equal-length strings, each string can be converted into a difference integer array of length n-1 , where each element in the difference array is calculated as the difference between consecutive letters in the alphabet.
statement: Given an array of equal-length strings, each string can be converted into a difference integer array of length n-1 , where each element in the difference array is calculated as the difference between consecutive letters in the alphabet. For example, the difference between 'a' and 'c' is 2. Among all the strings in the array, find the one whose difference integer array is unique.
constraints: A word’s difference signature contains each next character code minus the previous code.
Exactly one word has a signature different from every other word; return that word.
hints: Convert each word into its tuple of adjacent character-code differences.
Uniformly shifted words have identical difference tuples.
Count signatures and return the word whose signature occurs once.
The contract guarantees exactly one unique signature, so that lookup identifies the required word.
editorial: The contract guarantees exactly one unique signature, so that lookup identifies the required word.

tests.explanation: adc and wzy share differences [3,-1], while abc has [1,1], so abc is odd.
The constant-letter words share [0,0], while bob has [13,-13].
